passages.original: Trium namque rerum uel quotlibet tum genere tum specie tum numero diuersitas constat; quotiens enim idem dicitur, totiens diuersum etiam praedicatum Idem uero dicitur tribus modis: aut genere ut idem homo quod equus, quia his idem genus ut animal; uel specie ut idem Cato quod Cicero, quia, eadem species ut homo; uel numero ut Tullius et Cicero, quia unus est numero. Quare diuersum etiam uel genere uel specie uel numero dicitur. Sed numero differentiam accidentium uarietas facit. Nam tres homines neque genere neque specie sed suis acci de litibus distant;
passages.english: For the diversity of three things, or of any number whatever, consists in genus, or in species, or in number; for as often as "the same" is said, so often is "diverse" also predicated. Now "the same" is said in three ways: either by genus, as a man is the same as a horse, because they have the same genus, namely animal; or by species, as Cato is the same as Cicero, because [they have] the same species, namely man; or by number, as Tully and Cicero, because he is one in number. Therefore "diverse" is also said either by genus or by species or by number. But it is variety of accidents that makes difference in number. For three men differ neither by genus nor by species but by their accidents;
passages.notes: "acci de litibus" is a scanning error for "accidentibus" (accidents), translated as such. A full stop appears to be missing after "praedicatum".
